title: Frontline draws on Simon Allen's research to explain Himalayan glacial lake risk
summary: Frontline (The Hindu) examines the growing hazard from Himalayan glacial lakes in the wake of the Rasuwa flood, building its analysis on research led by Simon Allen modelling worst-case outburst scenarios in a transboundary basin. That work found flood waves reaching the Nepal border in roughly 30 minutes — too fast for early warning alone, and a case for coupling it with land-use planning.

title: Simon Allen contributes to Stimson Center analysis of the Rasuwa flood
summary: The Stimson Center published a rapid analysis of the August 2026 Rasuwa flood on the China–Nepal border, which killed more than 570 people. Simon Allen is credited among the collaborators who informed the assessment.

title: Simon Allen quoted on glacier collapse behind deadly Nepal flash flood
summary: Simon Allen was quoted in The Japan Times on the August 2026 flash flood in Nepal, which reporting attributes to a glacier collapse and ice avalanche. The coverage highlights the growing climate risk from cascading cryosphere hazards in the Himalaya.

title: Simon Allen quoted in Insurance Journal on the Nepal glacier collapse
summary: Insurance Journal carried Bloomberg's coverage of the August 2026 glacier collapse on the Nepal–China border, quoting Simon Allen on the ice-and-rock avalanche that fluidised into the flood, and on how retreating glaciers and thawing permafrost make such events more likely.

title: The Edge Malaysia carries Simon Allen's assessment of the Nepal disaster
summary: The Edge Malaysia ran the wire coverage of the Nepal–China glacier collapse, quoting Simon Allen on the ice-and-rock avalanche behind the flood and his assessment that it looks set to be the largest Himalayan disaster on record — one he hopes will prove a turning point.

title: Financial Times quotes Simon Allen on the forces behind the Himalayan flood
summary: The Financial Times examined the cascade of forces behind the deadly flood on the Nepal–China border in a piece titled “The devastating forces behind the deadly Himalayan flood”, with Simon Allen among the scientists quoted.

title: Erosion-driven shrinkage of glacier-detached lakes across the Third Pole
summary: Simon Allen co-authored a study in Global and Planetary Change showing that recently glacier-detached lakes across the Third Pole are shrinking through erosion, signalling a proglacial-to-paraglacial transition.

title: Collapsing mountains: where next, and how to avoid future disasters
summary: Simon Allen co-authored a paper in Geomorphology asking where the next catastrophic mountain collapse is likely and how such disasters can be avoided — questions given sharp relevance by the Rasuwa flood weeks later.

title: Indigenous Peoples and knowledge in National Adaptation Plans
summary: Simon Allen co-authored a survey of global mountain regions assessing how Indigenous Peoples and Indigenous knowledge are represented in National Adaptation Plans.

title: GLOF warning and evacuation experiences in Lunana, Bhutan
summary: A new paper in the International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction, co-authored by Simon Allen, examines public warning and evacuation experiences during the 2019 and 2023 glacial lake outburst flood events in Lunana, Bhutan, and draws recommendations for future preparedness.

title: Record-breaking glacier mass loss in Central Asia in 2025
summary: Joel Fiddes co-authored a new study documenting record-breaking glacier mass loss across Central Asia in 2025, published in Environmental Research Letters.

title: Advancing stakeholder engagement in climate adaptation
summary: Simon Allen co-authored a systematic review in Sustainability Science examining structural barriers and operational enablers for stakeholder engagement in climate adaptation.

title: SnowMapper data underpins hydrosolutions' Central Asia snow assessment
summary: hydrosolutions published an assessment of snow accumulation across the mountainous parts of the Syr Darya and Amu Darya basins for the 2025–26 season, drawing on SnowMapper model data to compare sub-basin snow levels against historical averages and the previous year.

title: EGU 2026: glacier mass changes in the Western Pamirs, 2003–2025
summary: Joel Fiddes co-authored an EGU 2026 presentation constraining glacier mass balance in the Western Pamirs from high-resolution stereo satellite imagery — a mountain water tower whose glaciers saw limited but accelerating loss through 2000–2019.

title: EGU 2026: modelling cascading hazards at Thame, Nepal
summary: Simon Allen co-authored an EGU 2026 presentation on modelling cascading hazards in high mountain environments, using the Thame case study in Nepal — where rock or ice failure above a glacial lake can set off a chain of secondary processes.

title: hydrosolutions' February 2026 snow assessment built on SnowMapper
summary: hydrosolutions assessed snow accumulation to the end of February 2026 across the mountainous Syr Darya and Amu Darya sub-basins, using SnowMapper model data for the Pskem, Chatkal, Vakhsh, Pyanj, Zeravshan and Kashkadarya catchments.

title: Advancing GLOF hazard assessment in Bhutan
summary: New NHESS study finds over 11,000 people exposed to glacial lake outburst flood risk in Bhutan through hydrodynamic flood mapping and exposure analysis. Simon Allen co-authored.

title: Snowmelt buffers drought in Nepal's Karnali basin
summary: Joel Fiddes co-authored a study in Frontiers in Water using a fully distributed hydrological model to show how snowmelt regulates streamflow in the upstream Karnali basin in Nepal, and what that means for downstream water supply and nature conservation.

title: GLOF risk modelling advances in Kyrgyz Republic
summary: New research published in NHESS compares lake lowering, deflection dams, and retention basins for managing glacial lake outburst flood risk in the Ala-Archa valley.

title: End-of-January 2026 snowpack assessment uses the SnowMapper model
summary: hydrosolutions reported on snowpack across the Syr Darya and Amu Darya basins for October 2025 to end of January 2026, drawing on the SnowMapper snow cover model for the Pskem and Chatkal basins that feed the Charvak reservoir.

title: New study: Mitigating future glacial lake outburst floods in the Himalaya
summary: Published in Science Bulletin, this study evaluates China's Glacial Lake Management System and finds that GLMS engineering could reduce flood intensity by 24%. Simon Allen contributed as co-author.

title: SnowMapper informs the 2025–26 season-opening Central Asia snow assessment
summary: hydrosolutions assessed snow accumulation for October to December 2025 across the mountainous Syr Darya and Amu Darya basins, with SnowMapper showing accumulation in the Pskem and Chatkal basins within the normal range.

title: TopoPyScale v0.3.3 released with critical bug fix
summary: TopoPyScale v0.3.3 fixes a critical bug where clustered pixels were not remapped to their correct locations, causing incorrect spatial output when using the clustering option.

title: TopoPyScale v0.3.1 released
summary: Latest release of our open-source Python library for hillslope-scale climate downscaling, now used by research groups worldwide for snow, permafrost, and hydrological modelling.

title: WMO Global Cryosphere Watch: Regional Snow Assessments 2025
summary: Joel Fiddes contributed to the GCW 2025 regional snow assessments, providing operational snow analysis for Central Asia as part of the WMO expert network.

title: CROMO-ADAPT enters final phase
summary: The CHF 2.96M SDC-funded project on cryospheric observation and modelling in Central Asia enters its final implementation phase, with operational tools now serving national hydrometeorological agencies.

title: SnowMapper used to time the onset of snowmelt in the Aral Sea basin
summary: hydrosolutions used SnowMapper data to identify that peak snow water equivalent had passed across the Aral Sea basin, marking the onset of the intensive snowmelt period across the Syr Darya and Amu Darya headwaters.

title: End-of-March 2025 snowpack assessment flags a poor season via SnowMapper
summary: hydrosolutions reported that SnowMapper showed snow reserves across the mountainous Syr Darya basin significantly below both the long-term average and the previous year, covering October 2024 to the end of March 2025.

title: SnowMapper completes second operational season
summary: SnowMapper CA completed its second full winter season covering 400,000+ km² across five Central Asian countries. The 2024–25 assessment documented anomalously low snow in the Syr Darya basin.
